task: Build a new local-first freelance finance tracker phone app with Expo (React Native) for iOS and Android. Privacy is the product: all of the user's data stays on their device. There is no server, no accounts, no sign-up or login, no analytics, tracking or crash reporting, and the app never sends user data anywhere. Must-haves: (1) Policy agreement gate: on first launch, and whenever the policy version changes, the user must read the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy and tick "I agree" before anything else in the app is reachable; acceptance (policy version and date) is stored on the device. The policy says plainly that data stays on the device and the developer never receives it, that the user is responsible for their own backups, and that the app is not tax, legal or financial advice. (2) Receipts: photograph with the camera (photo-library fallback) and record amount, date, category, type (expense by default, or income) and notes; photos are kept in the app's private storage. (3) Mileage log: date, miles and purpose, with the deduction at a configurable rate per mile (default: the current IRS standard business rate, labeled "verify for your tax year"). (4) Dashboard: income, expenses, mileage deduction and estimated tax at a configurable rate (never negative), recent activity, and every primary action one tap away. (5) Exports: tax-ready CSV and PDF generated on the device and shared through the share sheet. (6) Encrypted on-device storage: the database is encrypted at rest with a key kept in the device keychain/keystore (expo-secure-store). (7) Backup and restore: export one encrypted backup file containing all records and photos, protected by a passphrase the user chooses (strong key derivation and authenticated encryption from an audited JavaScript library such as @noble/ciphers and @noble/hashes), shared wherever the user chooses (Files, iCloud Drive, Google Drive); restore from such a file with the passphrase after a clear confirmation, with an integrity check and a friendly message for a wrong passphrase or damaged file. Cloud-provider sync is out of scope for now. (8) Optional app lock with Face ID, Touch ID or fingerprint (expo-local-authentication), OFF by default and switchable in Settings. (9) Settings: app lock, mileage rate, tax rate, backup and restore, view the policy, and delete all data (with confirmation). The app must be visually appealing, polished and very easy to use: React Native Paper (Material 3) with a theme and shared components, generous spacing, a clear visual hierarchy, friendly empty states and a bottom tab bar to every main area. Use the current Expo SDK (look up versions with npm view; never guess). Includes unit and integration tests of the on-device logic.

ui.summary: The app largely follows the DESIGN.md specification – all screens and their required states exist, navigation via the bottom tab bar and FAB provides access to every primary action, headings and landmarks are correctly used, and the accessibility audit reports an A‑score of 98 with zero axe violations. Design tokens are leveraged in most components, and the mobile‑first layout (390 dp width, 16 dp horizontal padding, 8 dp vertical rhythm) is respected. However, a critical regression blocks the primary restore‑backup flow: the "Select backup file" button never triggers a file picker, breaking the end‑to‑end data‑restore path. Several medium‑severity gaps remain – backup‑passphrase validation is not enforced, focus‑visible outlines are missing on many interactive components, a few UI elements still use hard‑coded colors/sizes instead of the theme, and temporary backup files are not cleaned up. Low‑severity security concerns (missing CSP header on the web build and encryption key stored in localStorage) are also noted. These issues should be addressed before the app is deemed production‑ready.

findings.issue: The "Select backup file" button never opens a file chooser on web, causing the Restore flow to time‑out (step 65). The flow is required by the spec and its failure prevents users from restoring backups.
findings.fix: Replace the current button with a proper `<input type="file" />` element (or use expo‑document‑picker with web support). Ensure the onPress handler programmatically clicks the hidden file input and handles the selected file via FileReader. Add appropriate `accept` attribute and test the flow on both web and native.

findings.issue: Backup passphrase UI hints at a minimum of 8 characters but the validation logic does not enforce this; the "Create backup" button can be enabled with a weak or mismatching passphrase.
findings.fix: Add client‑side validation that checks both fields for a length >= 8 and matching values before enabling the button. Show a `HelperText` error when the requirement is not met, and disable the button with a visible disabled style.

findings.issue: Buttons lack a visible focus outline on native platforms (focus‑visible style is only applied on web). This violates WCAG 2.1 §2.4.7 for keyboard focus indication.
findings.fix: Add a `style` prop that applies a 2 dp `outline` using `theme.colors.outline` when `props.focused` (or via `onFocus`/`onBlur` state) on both web and native. Ensure the touch target remains ≥ 44 × 44 dp.

findings.issue: Some components use hard‑coded spacing (e.g., `marginBottom: 16` or `padding: 12`) instead of the `theme.spacing` token, which deviates from the design‑token‑only rule and makes the 8 dp vertical rhythm inconsistent.
findings.fix: Refactor all static margin/padding values to use `theme.spacing * n` (or `theme.roundness` for border‑radius). Update the StyleSheet definitions to reference the token object.

findings.issue: The Save button is disabled until the form is valid, but the disabled state provides no visual cue (colour or opacity) and no accessible `aria-disabled` description, which can confuse users and may be considered a silently disabled submit.
findings.fix: Apply a distinct disabled style (e.g., reduced opacity, `theme.colors.disabled` background) and set `accessibilityState={{ disabled: true }}` on the button. Add a helper text explaining why the button is disabled (e.g., "All fields must be completed.").

findings.issue: The encryption key for the web fallback is persisted in `localStorage`, violating the local‑first security model and exposing encrypted data to any script with access to storage.
findings.fix: Either disable the web build for production or replace the storage mechanism with an in‑memory key derived from a user‑provided passphrase for the session. If persistence is required, store only a key‑derivation salt and never the raw key.

findings.issue: The web build does not include a Content‑Security‑Policy header, leaving the SPA vulnerable to XSS if a future DOM injection occurs.
findings.fix: Add a CSP meta tag to `public/index.html` (or configure the static host to send an HTTP CSP header) that restricts scripts to `'self'` and disallows `unsafe-inline`.

findings.issue: Backup files are written to a static cache path (`cacheDirectory/backup.bak`) and are not deleted after the share sheet completes, resulting in leftover encrypted files on the device.
findings.fix: Generate a unique temporary filename for each backup, invoke `FileSystem.deleteAsync` after `Sharing.shareAsync` resolves, and handle any errors gracefully.

findings.issue: Form design lacks labels above fields (as per spec, this is a policy screen, not an entry form, but the design should still follow form principles).
findings.fix: Add labels above each field or use placeholder text if labels aren't applicable.

findings.issue: No error states shown for checkbox or button — the screen only shows a disabled button, which is insufficient for a polished product.
findings.fix: Show validation message (e.g., 'Please agree to terms') when checkbox is unchecked.

findings.issue: The 'Accept' button is centered and lacks visual emphasis — it should be the primary action and stand out more.
findings.fix: Increase button size, add a subtle shadow or border, and make the text bold.

findings.issue: Content is tightly aligned to the left edge with no right padding or margin — feels cramped and unpolished for desktop.
findings.fix: Add generous horizontal padding (e.g., 24px) on both sides to create breathing room.

findings.issue: No vertical spacing between sections — the policy text block and checkbox are too close together.
findings.fix: Add 16–24px vertical spacing between the policy block and checkbox to improve readability.

findings.issue: The 'Tick the box above to continue' message is redundant — it’s implied by the disabled button.
findings.fix: Remove or replace with a more concise message like 'Agree to continue'.

observations: validator 'ui primary flow (.)' blocked 6 of 6 rounds
coder hit its turn limit in 2 of 6 rounds ([1, 5])

went_well: All unit and integration tests passed in every round, confirming that core business logic and data handling were correct.
The designer delivered a complete ui_flow.json and DESIGN.md within 6 calls, giving the coder a clear navigation map.
Vision model scores remained stable (average ~7.0) across the run, showing consistent visual quality of the UI mock‑ups.
Static reviewers caught high‑severity security issues and disallowed raw HTML components, keeping the codebase on a secure baseline.
Round and coder turn limits prevented unbounded token usage; only two turn‑limit hits occurred despite a large number of calls.

improvements.title: Make UI primary‑flow validator tolerant and more diagnostic for file‑picker and export actions
improvements.evidence: Rounds 1‑6 all failed on validator "ui primary flow (.)". Round 1 & 6: "upload button 'Select backup file' failed: page.waitForEvent: Timeout 10000ms". Rounds 3‑5: "click button 'Export'" produced "Maximum call stack size exceeded". Round 6: validator noted use of experimental `window.showOpenFilePicker` which does not fire Playwright's `filechooser` event.
improvements.change: Modify ui_check.mjs to (a) recognize Expo DocumentPicker/WebFileInput patterns and treat a successful `DocumentPicker.getDocumentAsync` as a valid file‑chooser event, (b) add a fallback detection for a visible `<input type='file'>` element, and (c) surface the exact component identifier (file, line, accessibilityLabel) with a clear "expected‑behavior vs. observed" diff in the failure report.
improvements.expected_effect: Coder can implement a compliant file‑picker and export button in one focused edit, eliminating repeated UI‑flow failures and cutting the number of rounds needed to clear validator "ui primary flow".

improvements.title: Add static validator for circular exports and recursive component registration
improvements.evidence: Round 5 error: "Got an invalid value for 'component' prop for the screen 'Restore'. It must be a React component… infinite‑recursive getter" caused by `src/screens/RestoreScreen.web.tsx` re‑exporting its own default and `src/navigation/index.tsx` registering that as a screen. This circular export triggered UI validator failures at step 46.
improvements.change: Extend validate.py with a new check named `detect_circular_exports` that parses ES6 export statements, flags re‑exports that resolve to the same file (or create import cycles) and reports the offending file/line. Include this check in the static‑validation pipeline before UI validation runs.
improvements.expected_effect: Circular import bugs are caught early, preventing runtime navigation crashes and the subsequent UI‑flow validator blocks, thus saving coder iterations.

improvements.title: Introduce pre‑coding dependency vulnerability guard
improvements.evidence: Round 3 security scan reported high‑severity unfixed vulnerabilities in `braces@3.0.3`, `node-forge@1.4.0`, `sprintf-js@1.0.3` and a medium‑severity issue in `uuid@7.0.3`. Because security findings are blocking, the coder later had to replace or upgrade these packages, adding extra work.
improvements.change: Add a pre‑run step in the planner phase that runs `npm audit` (or uses a curated CVE whitelist) and produces a "Dependency Constraints" document. Update the planner prompt to require selection of only vetted packages and disallow known vulnerable ones, offering alternatives (e.g., use `@noble/ciphers` instead of `node-forge`). Also add a static validator rule that flags imports of disallowed packages.
improvements.expected_effect: Vulnerable dependencies are avoided from the start, eliminating later security‑scanner blocks and reducing the need for mid‑run refactoring.

improvements.title: Refine reviewer prompt to require precise, actionable fix instructions
improvements.evidence: Reviewer feedback was sometimes vague: e.g., round 2 "remove the unused WebFileInput.web.tsx and replace the <button>..." but the coder still left problematic picker logic; round 5 mentioned an "infinite‑recursive getter" without showing the exact code change needed.
improvements.change: Update the reviewer prompt to mandate that each issue include (a) exact file path and line numbers, (b) a minimal before/after code snippet that resolves the failure, and (c) a brief rationale linking the snippet to the validator error. Enforce this format in the reviewer output.
improvements.expected_effect: Coder receives unambiguous, line‑level guidance, reducing guesswork and the number of revision rounds needed to satisfy validators.

improvements.title: Enhance coder turn‑limit feedback with a prioritized issue summary
improvements.evidence: Coder hit its turn limit in rounds 1 and 5, after which the only feedback was a generic "revise" flag. No concise list of remaining blockers was presented, leading to scattered edits and high token consumption (≈14 M prompt tokens).
improvements.change: When the coder turn‑limit guard triggers, automatically generate a "Turn‑Limit Report" that lists (1) all failing validators, (2) the specific UI steps or files causing each failure, and (3) a suggested order of remediation. Attach this report to the feedback message sent to the coder for the next round.
improvements.expected_effect: Coder can focus on the most critical blockers in a structured way, avoid sprawling changes, reduce token usage, and converge faster.
